description: Agent Cybersecurity: submit a secrets inventory with its policy: the policy with the most days allowed between rotations, the store it names (a vault or secrets manager), the days between reviews of the store’s access log, and its text; each secret with its id, name, kind (an API key, a token, a password, a certificate, a signing key, a database credential or other), where it is kept as recorded (a vault, a secrets manager, a key management service, an environment variable, a config file, code, a plain file, a document, a chat or not known), the store’s name, and the days it was created and last rotated; optionally each secret the recorded scan found in code or plain files, with its id, location, the inventory secret it is, the day found and whether it was removed; whether access to the secrets store is logged and when that log was last reviewed; and the day the record is read on. The signed report gives every secret with its kind, store and age, the secrets in a store, in plain locations, in environment variables or config files and in another store than the policy names, the rotations overdue, the scan findings still in place and the found secrets not rotated since, and the store access log with its review age, and counts them, and names exposed secrets: a secret kept in code, a plain file, a document or a chat, a scan finding still in place, a secret the scan found that was not rotated after it was found, and access to the secrets store that is not logged; then secrets in environment variables or config files, secrets in a store the policy does not name, rotation older than the policy allows and a store access log past its review cycle, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No inventory, a secret with no store, no rotation age in the policy, no day read on, a secret with no rotation or creation day, no scan record or no word on store logging leaves the secrets unverified. This reads secrets storage and rotation records: wever_onboarding-credential-check reads the credentials one new agent was issued and scans supplied text for credential strings, while the secrets check reads the inventory’s rotation ages against the policy, the recorded scan’s findings and the store’s own access log; wever_credential-requirements-check reads the credentials a listing asks for before payment and wever_single-credential-issue issues a verified single credential. Verdict cyber_secrets_exposed, cyber_secrets_partial, cyber_secrets_unverified or cyber_secrets_protected. POST /api/cyber-secrets-check. Reads the security records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, system scan, probe or external write. Agent Cybersecurity reads an organization’s own security records after the fact and checks them against the stated policy and against themselves: standing access, the secrets inventory, the component and patch record, the exported configuration, logging coverage, backup and restore evidence, a vendor’s security evidence and incident readiness. Beside it, the Agent Risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check read one planned action’s worst case and limits before it runs, while a cyber check reads security posture from the records; and the security reads elsewhere in the catalog keep their families, each named beside the check it meets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-cybersecurity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-cybersecurity/.

as_of.description: The day the records are read on, such as 2026-11-02.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

log_review_days.description: Days between reviews of the secrets store access log.

scan.description: Each secret the recorded scan found in code or plain files.

location.description: Where the scan found the secret, such as a repository path.

removed.description: Whether the secret was removed from that location.

rotated_on.description: When it was last rotated, such as 2026-11-02.

stored_in.description: Where the secret is kept, as recorded.

logged.description: Whether access to the secrets store is logged.

reviewed_on.description: When the access log was last reviewed, such as 2026-11-02.
